messages:
andrea: heads-up — after pushing BMC fw v2.4.8 to ap-south1 canary racks i'm seeing OOB session flaps + thermal sensor jitter. GPU provision failures started ~07:12 UTC.
infra-bot: [alert] oob-session-drop threshold breached (ap-south1). link: https://metrics.redwood/alerts/ALRT-9221 :rotating_light:
andrea: paste logs for one node: 
```
[07:12:03] bmc: fw v2.4.8 applied
[07:12:05] sensor: temp read 42C
[07:12:05] sensor: temp read 85C
[07:12:05] oob: session disconnected, reason=uart-reset
[07:12:07] bios: nvram write, key=bootflags
[07:12:09] gpu-provision: warmboot loop detected
```
mike: rough scope? how many racks/nodes affected?
andrea: canary group = r-a1..r-a6 primarily. approx 180 GPUs affected, ~12 nodes unrecoverable currently. spillover into preprod pools causing queuing.
ben: curious if this is secure-boot flip-related or nvram corruption after flash? any evidence of secureboot toggles?
andrea: no explicit secure-boot status flips in logs, but nvram write immediately after BMC fw apply looks suspicious. could be a write ordering bug. not seeing signature errors.
ops-runbook: recommend immediate actions: 1) PAUSE rollout, 2) ROLLBACK to v2.4.6 on canary, 3) mark affected racks for manual repro/offline maintenance, 4) drain GPUs and shift workloads away.
mike: agree pause + rollback. can someone start drains now? we should avoid mass eviction across region to prevent cost surge.
andrea: starting drains on r-a1..r-a6: command: `fleetctl drain --racks r-a1,r-a2,r-a3,r-a4,r-a5,r-a6 --reason "oob fw instability"`
ben: also throttle autoscaler in ap-south1 to prevent aggressive spin-up in other regions (cost). put a cap on burst to 10% for the next 2 hours.
andrea: throttling autoscaler now: `infractl set-burst-cap ap-south1 10% --ttl 2h`
sre-oncall: i'll take customer-facing impact triage and open incident channel if any SLOs are violated. pinging product and cs after we confirm rollback.
infra-bot: [deploy-bot] rollout paused by andrea at 07:24 UTC. rollback job queued (job id=rb-6160001).
andrea: starting rollback to 2.4.6 for canary. ETA ~15m. will update when complete.
mike: post-rollback checklist: 1) verify nvram persistence behavior, 2) run stress on thermal sensor reads, 3) reproduce nvram write ordering. add new test to fw CI.
en.wikipedia: kidding (ignore)
ben: also capture serial console dump for one of the failed nodes and attach to the ticket. helps FW team.
andrea: attaching console dump and creating ticket: https://issues.redwood/TKT-4021 — notes: intermittent uart resets, nvram writes within 2s post-flash.
ops-runbook: tag: urgent-fw-investigation. suggest escalation to vendor if rollback doesn't stabilize in 30m.
andrea: rollback finished on canary (07:39 UTC). initial checks: oob sessions stable on r-a1..r-a6, thermal reads back to normal pattern. marking rollout paused and creating hotfix branch for fw team.
sre-oncall: monitoring SLOs and capacity. current effective capacity in ap-south1 down ~8% due to drained racks, rebalancing compute from eu-west and usw3. estimated additional cross-region egress/cost ~+$420/hr if we keep long-term.
andrea: understood — will coordinate with finance if we need extended cross-region. next steps: full postmortem runbook entry, add nvram ordering test, vendor escalation if repro on 2.4.6 can't be replicated.
ben: great. also add a temp check in rollout automation to watch for >3 uart-resets in 5m and auto-pause.
andrea: adding automation check now.
infra-bot: [note] incident TKT-4021 created and linked to thread.
andrea: assigning owners: andrea (lead), ben (fw triage), mike (capacity), sre-oncall (customer/slo). will follow up in #incidents with postmortem. :white_check_mark:
